Subject: Authorization papertrail & SCIM sample request — Medivance SOC2 prep

Hi Kimberly,

As part of our SOC 2 evidence collection window, our audit team asked for a short set of artifacts showing how user-to-role bindings are represented in your SCIM exports and a sampling of SAML assertions for cross-validation. Specifically we need:

- A SCIM user/role snapshot (CSV or JSON) showing role assignments for the last quarterly snapshot
- A few (3–5) SAML assertion samples for federated logins that include role/attribute claims
- An export of your RBAC role list with descriptions (role name, permissions summary)

Can you confirm whether you can provide redacted artifacts (user identifiers hashed) or if you need us to accept masked CSVs? We have a compliance cutoff next Tuesday and would like to include these in the evidence bundle.

Big picture: the auditors are trying to validate least-privilege mapping and that role changes are traceable to owners. If you can also include the mapping of attribute names used in SAML (e.g., eduPersonAffiliation or custom role claim) that would save us time.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-minute call if helpful.

Best,
Elaine Murray
Senior Security Manager
Medivance Health

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you asked for with some standard redaction. Quick answers up front:

- SCIM snapshot: we can produce a CSV export of user -> role assignments for the snapshot date; we will hash user ids and include a role id column and role name.
- SAML assertions: we can share 3 redacted assertion examples (timestamped, with issuer and attribute claims) — we will blank out NameID but keep attribute keys/values intact where needed for mapping.
- RBAC export: we will include a JSON role catalogue (role id, name, description, privilege summary) and a small table that maps role id -> canonical permissions.

Two quick clarifying questions so we deliver what your auditors expect:
1) For the SCIM snapshot, do you prefer a full-attribute view (all mapped attributes) or a condensed export with only user_id, role_id, role_name, assigned_at?
2) Do auditors need signed SAML traces (raw XML) or are sanitized copies acceptable?

Proposed timeline: we can turn the artifacts around by EOD Thursday (2026-08-13) if we get confirmation on the two points above. If you want a walkthrough of how the exports were generated we can schedule a short call.

I’m looping in Jordan (IAM) and Sean (Security) to help assemble the artifacts and ensure redaction meets your needs.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

Kimberly —

Condensed SCIM snapshot is fine (user_hash, role_id, role_name, assigned_at). Sanitized SAML XML is acceptable as long as the attribute names and values we need are present. For RBAC, the JSON role catalogue works.

Please include a short readme (plain text) that documents how the snapshot was extracted (tool/version, snapshot timestamp) and the hashing algorithm used for user identifiers. The auditors want reproducibility notes.

If you can share the artifacts to a secure Drive link and reply-all with the link we will pull them into our tracker. Target for us is to attach them to the SOC 2 evidence packet by Friday COB, so your EOD Thursday turnaround is perfect.

Thanks for looping Jordan and Sean.

—Elaine

Notes on redaction: auditors want attribute names left intact. Do not remove custom role claim keys. Mask all PII (email addresses, employee IDs) via deterministic hash so auditors can correlate if needed.

Please confirm ETA on each item in this thread.

Thanks — Kimberly
